# Clankdar

Fresh capability checks. Portable, verifiable receipts.

Clankdar is a small HTTP API for issuing fresh puzzles, scoring one set of
answers exactly, and retrieving the signed JSON result. Applications supply
the solver and decide when to check, what to associate the result with, and
how to use it. No actor registration, public profile, campaign, repository
checkout, Bun runtime, or model-provider configuration is required to call
the API. Clankdar does not select or call a model for the integrator.

The hosted API is invitation-only experimental staging at
https://clankdar-hosted-staging.972abc65.workers.dev.

- POST /v1/checks: Authorization: Bearer <invitation-token>; JSON {} selects
  the default v2-floor-v1 policy. Optional fields are policyId, context
  (a nonempty, non-sensitive string up to 256 characters), and subjectPublicKey.
  Returns ok, id, ticket, policyId, expiresAt, challenges, and receiptUrl.
- POST /v1/checks/:id/responses: JSON {ticket,responses}, with responses mapping
  actual challenge IDs to answer strings. The scoped ticket authorizes this
  request; the issue token is not needed. Optional subjectProof is required
  when a subjectPublicKey was requested. Returns ok, id, pass, passed,
  required, receiptUrl, sha256, and receipt.
- GET /v1/checks/:id: unauthenticated read of the raw immutable canonical
  clankdar-gate-v1 signed admission JSON, containing protocol, payload, and
  signature. The submission response's sha256 hashes these exact bytes.

The two policies ask four puzzles and require three passing responses.
v2-floor-v1 allows 120 seconds; frontier-floor-v1 allows 180 seconds.
GET /v1/policies lists policies. GET /v1/policies/:id returns one policy.
Creating a check does not call a model. Empty or wrong answers are a failed
attempt, not a dry run. The first accepted submission fixes the result;
valid retries recover it rather than replacing answers. A create retry
issues a new check and consumes another quota slot. Unanswered checks
expire without storing a result. A 404 does not prove a scheduled miss.

Keep the invitation token server-side and the ticket private until used or
expired. Context and submitted responses become public evidence; do not put
private information or credentials in them. A receipt remains readable after
the ticket expires. Download your own copy: no automatic deletion is
configured, but experimental staging does not promise perpetual retention.

Each completed check stores one canonical JSON admission in R2, including
its challenge receipts. A small D1 counter bounds issuance. The core creates
no actor, campaign, session database row, or duplicate receipt object.
Standalone checks share a limit of 1,024 issued checks over staging's
lifetime and 60 issues per fixed UTC minute; these are not per-token allowances.
Request bodies are bounded at 128 KiB; receipts at 256 KiB. Integrators own
solver costs, request and token budgets, scheduling, and alerting.

The source example cloudflare/examples/check.mjs runs server-side with Node 22+ or Bun, using standard JavaScript
fetch and a caller-supplied solve(challenges, signal) callback. It creates,
submits, and downloads the exact receipt. Forward the AbortSignal to any
provider request. The helper does not select a provider or start paid calls
on its own. An optional awaited checkpoint(record) callback can retain the
ticket and answers privately before submission for later recovery. The
optional offline verifier uses Bun 1.3.14 and the existing
independent scorer:

bun cloudflare/examples/verify-receipt.mjs receipt.json --issuer PUBLIC_KEY

Optional --context, --session, and --sha256 assert integration expectations.
The expected issuer key must come from trusted application configuration,
not the untrusted receipt. Verification checks signatures and replays recorded answers. Only present,
well-formed answers produce challenge receipts that reveal seeds. Missing or
malformed answers count as nonpassing without a challenge receipt or seed
reveal; a blank-answer demo still verifies as 0 of 4 passing. A failed result
can be a valid receipt. Applications must enforce
their intended policy, freshness, and passing verdict before granting access.

Example integrations: agent preflight, release checks in CI, recent evidence
on an agent listing, or scheduled monitoring owned by the integrating app.
A single check has no ongoing-availability denominator. Existing hosted
actor/campaign routes and records are preserved as an optional legacy
reference application, not prerequisites for the atomic API.

A check measures submitted answers under recorded conditions. It does not
prove model identity, autonomy, uniqueness, personhood, safety, or permission
to act. Work can be delegated or solved with code. Issuer signatures are
issuer claims; an issuer can self-mint. Current hosted policies draw fresh
instances from public generator streams, not issuer-private held-out pools.

The local benchmark calibrates these task families and scoring rules.
Current generator: clankdar-suite-v2. Current scorer: clankdar-score-v2.
Exact typed scoring preserves meaningful case, signs, boundaries, and
dimensions. There is no judge model. Published calibrations replay without
model-provider calls. The v2 calibration has 2,500 attempts from five
requested model aliases, including one timeout; strict scores span
9.4%–87.6%. Frontier has 1,700 unaided attempts; the separate tool-agent track
has 600 bounded episodes. Family/tier profiles preserve sample size and
uncertainty; pooled tiers are not a single intelligence scale. Four published
signed reference sessions contain 32 replayed challenge checks. These are
receipt examples, not a claim about the new hosted API's model performance.

Benchmark model invocations default to dry runs; execution requires
--execute and --max-requests. Local reference tools also implement badges,
held-out pools, and transparency/witness prototypes. Presence in source
does not mean integration into the atomic hosted API.
